dedupe_keys.name: 5g high density demand hdd dataset in liverpool city region uk

description: Liverpool John Moores University and CGA Simulations produced the 5G High Density Demand dataset to examine wireless service at two Liverpool event venues. It contains simulated user locations, traffic classes, radio-unit associations, signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios, physical resource block use, throughput and block error rates. Salt and Tar contains 3,000 users and the ACC Arena contains 12,000 users, with 10,000 samples in the released sequences. The repository dates collection from 3 March to 13 June 2025; it does not state a uniform sampling interval on its landing page. CSV tables in a ZIP package and README documentation are published through the LJMU repository, with an open Zenodo mirror. The stated CC BY 4.0 licence permits free reuse with attribution. These are digital-twin and simulator outputs checked against measurements, not a continuous operational network trace. They can support capacity planning, demand modelling and digital-twin comparisons for dense venues. The generating workflow uses the Vienna 5G system-level simulator, catalogued as model-vienna-5g-simulators; obtaining all of the workflow's code requires separate access arrangements.
